title: Personal Checking Settings for a Balance That Stays Negative
content:
Where a Personal Checking account's ledger balance stays below zero, three settings of the tier govern what follows: the one-time charge for a negative episode that has run long enough, the number of consecutive calendar days of negative balance that triggers that charge, and the numbers of consecutive calendar days after which the account is restricted and after which the deficit is charged off.

| Tier | One-time charge per negative episode (USD) | Consecutive calendar days of negative balance after which that charge applies | Consecutive calendar days after which the account is restricted | Consecutive calendar days after which the deficit is charged off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Private Client Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |

A charge of 0.00 means the tier writes no such charge however long the balance stays negative; the restriction and charge-off day counts still apply on every tier.

**Ordering of the three day counts.** Every tier reads the same three lengths from the day the balance first went negative: 7 calendar days for the one-time charge, 30 for restriction and 60 for charge-off. An episode cured before day 7 reaches none of them.
